thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE - multiple alerts for elevated packet loss and BGP route churn to upstream provider 'TransitOne' affecting us-east-1 (Ashburn) egress. Severity: potential customer impact. Please acknowledge.

Lara: acked. I'm oncall and looking. seeing alerts from both net-metrics and api-gateway.

SRE-Oncall: I see it too. Spike in 5xx from edge -> backend over last 6m. Traces show increased latency then resets.

Anand: I'm pulling BGP telemetry now. Noting rapid AS path changes for several /22s announced by TransitOne, prepending + withdraws.

Mike: Customer success pinged — a handful of enterprise customers in VA are seeing timeouts for embed and chat endpoints. They said retry helps.

Kirsten: Can we check if DNS resolution is converging to alternate providers or if it's purely transport?

Anand: quick traceroutes from two ashburn edge hosts:
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  ash-edge-a (10.240.1.12)  0.35 ms  0.29 ms  0.26 ms
 2  transit1-core (198.51.100.1)  12.5 ms  11.9 ms  12.2 ms
 3  transit1-peering (198.51.100.5)  62.1 ms  63.3 ms  200 ms
 4  * * *
```
Anand: see that big jump and then timeouts. Some flows get massive RTT then drop.

Lara: looks like TransitOne side is flapping/blackholing after a certain hop. Any BGP table snapshots?

Anand: yes — from our route-collector:
```
Network         Next Hop        AS_PATH
203.0.113.0/22   198.51.100.1    65001 65099 65050 65010
203.0.113.0/22   198.51.101.1    65002 65050 65100
```
Anand: We started seeing alternating next-hops within minutes. TransitOne's peer ASN shows different prepends.

SRE-Oncall: Immediate mitigation idea: steer critical prefixes off TransitOne by setting local-preference for backup provider and announce more specific /24s to prefer backup. Pros: quick traffic shift. Cons: more specific announcement churn and potential collateral. Thoughts?

Mike: CS says top 3 customers are latency-sensitive, make sure we notify them if we tilt traffic.

Kirsten: Also check DNS TTLs — if we shift egress region, CDN/edge IPs may still resolve to ashburn and hit failing paths. Might need coord with CDN edge steering.

Lara: On it. I'm opening provider ticket with TransitOne now: "AS65010 intermittent route withdrawals and high packet loss — please triage". Sending them logs and traceroutes.

Lara: Ticket created -> TICKET-18923. Sent BGP AS path dumps, timestamps, sample pcap from ash-edge-b.

IncidentBot: Note: Incident incident-2071002468 created and linked to TICKET-18923. PagerDuty escalation triggered to NetOps.

Anand: Implementing emergency traffic steering: 1) announce /24 specifics for the affected /22s via BackupTransit (AS65100) with higher localpref, 2) set communities to prefer backup on our routers. Pushing config now.

SRE-Oncall: Please post the exact commands you push. Need to audit for rollback.

Anand: Pushed snippet to ashburn-bgp: 
```
router bgp 65010
  neighbor 198.51.101.1 route-map STEER-TO-BACKUP out
route-map STEER-TO-BACKUP permit 10
  set local-preference 200
  match ip address prefix-list AFFECTED
ip prefix-list AFFECTED seq 5 permit 203.0.113.0/22
```

Anand: backing off /24 hack — instead used route-map + localpref to prefer backup on egress. Waiting for convergence.

Kirsten: Watching global egress percentages. Cloud metrics show ashburn egress to TransitOne drop from 60% -> 12% in ~45s. Good.

Ruben: I'm rotating logs for the affected frontends and adjusting alert thresholds to avoid noise while we stabilize.

Mike: FYI customers report improved error rates after ~2m of the change. One still seeing intermittent failures.

Lara: Could be session affinity hitting a bad path. We may need a short connection drain window (60s) for LB sessions in ashburn.

SRE-Oncall: Initiating connection-drain: `balancerctl drain ashburn-edge-a --timeout 60s` on affected nodes.

Anand: TransitOne responded: "We've seen a partial outage on our SFO->IAD backbone segment, engineering are investigating, temporary traffic engineering applied." They asked for sample pcap and BGP logs — sent.

Kirsten: Any DNS anomalies? I checked our resolver logs — no increased NXDOMAIN, just increased timeouts correlated with packet loss windows. So not DNS propagation.

Ruben: Customer impact summary so far (quick): ~11 customers got transient 5xx spikes, 4 enterprise accounts opened support tickets, no data loss. Most recovered after reroute.

Mike: Communicating to CS: short update to impacted customers: we rerouted traffic away from TransitOne in ashburn while they investigate; expect degraded latency but improved reliability.

Lara: Toggle autoscale on some edge pool nodes to handle re-routed load — increasing capacity by +12 nodes for 20m window.

SRE-Oncall: Monitoring metrics. Key watch: tokengen latency, 5xx rate, TCP retransmit %, BGP route flaps count.

Anand: Flap count down from 18/min -> 2/min after steer. TransitOne still has higher error counters but not collapsing.

IncidentBot: Update: pager status -> acknowledged, mitigation in progress, severity lowered to P2 due to limited customer impact after steering.

Kirsten: Recommend follow-up: 1) request postmortem from TransitOne, 2) schedule a peering review with them, 3) add route dampening thresholds for these ASN paths.

Lara: Agreed. I'll own the customer comms and run the post-incident RCA with NetOps tomorrow. Assigning action items:
- Lara: customer comm + RCA owner
- Anand: vendor logs + BGP dump archive (TICKET-18923)
- SRE-Oncall: monitor and revert steering when stable
- Ruben: rotate alerts and update runbook with steering steps

Mike: Thanks team. If TransitOne confirms it's resolved we'll start bringing traffic back gradually using traffic ramp policy (10% every 5m).

Anand: marking config changes and timestamps in change log. Rollback plan ready: remove STEER-TO-BACKUP route-map and re-evaluate.

Lara: closing the active paging once we get stable metrics for 30m. For now keeping incident open.

SRE-Oncall: ack. continuing watch.

IncidentBot: Incident 2071002468 state: mitigation applied -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 15 minutes or on any regressions. :white_check_mark:
